meetings.title: Kickoff + Intro Session: Let's Get Started
goals: Form the team and understand the Explore Story, season journey, and Core Values
Launch all season paperwork with families
Establish roles and material-management routine
activities: Walk through the wordless Explore Story comic (intro deck slides 2-4)
Present the team journey: challenge -> Core Values -> team model via Explore/Create/Test/Share -> poster -> festival
Introduce the 7 rotating team roles (+optional Team Captain)
Write team name and all member names on Engineering Notebook p.3; write season goals on p.6 (START HERE)
Introduce the six Core Values and the p.7 draw/write page
Show the BIOGLOW Explore Set and set the material routine; watch a BIOGLOW season playlist video
Send home consent/registration forms; communicate Tue/Thu cadence and festival plan to families
deliverables: EN p.3 team name + roster complete
EN p.6 season goals written
Consent forms distributed; meeting schedule communicated to families

meetings.title: Session 1: Canopy Connections
goals: Explore the BIOGLOW theme and share biodiversity knowledge
Build the tree model
Introduce Core Value: Discovery
activities: Discovery intro 5-10 min (TMG p.5 definition; draw example on EN p.7)
Vocabulary: biodiversity, canopy, habitat; guiding questions on the Explore Story (EN p.4); write/draw on p.8
Build the tree model (Book 1, Bags 1-3) after sorting groups 1-9
Discuss rainforest layers (EN p.30) and which animals live floor vs canopy; draw animals on p.9
Challenge: rearrange the leaves to make a specific habitat
Share to the room; Career Connection: Wildlife Biologist; clean up — KEEP tree assembled
deliverables: Tree model built and stored assembled
Discovery example on Core Values page

meetings.title: Session 2: Creature Creators
goals: Build all Explore Set animals and invent new ones
Introduce Core Value: Impact
activities: Recap + vocabulary (camouflage, behaviors); Impact intro 5-10 min with EN p.7 drawing
Split into pairs and build the three animals (Book 2, Bags 4-6); label animal parts in notebooks
Lay out the Explore mat, decide where each animal lives, tell a story about one animal
Challenge: trade pieces to invent a new animal — name, diet, movement, mat home
Share differences between animals; clean up: fold/store mat, CHARGE the SPIKE set
Collect signed consent forms from families
deliverables: All animal models built
Signed consent forms coming in

meetings.title: Coding readiness: SPIKE app Tutorial Activities
goals: Prepare a coding-new team before Session 3 (TMG recommendation)
Verify device, app, and hub setup
activities: Run SPIKE app Tutorial Activities as a team (TMG pre-season/Session 3 tip for teams new to coding)
Verify SPIKE app + FIRST LEGO League Explore Unit access on the team device; update and charge the hub
Core Values example-banking (5-10 min): record concrete teamwork moments so far
Team-building game and goal-setting videos (How To Set Goals 4:40 / SMART goals 2:52) from the Multimedia Resources
deliverables: Device + Explore Unit lessons verified working
Hub updated and fully charged for Session 3

meetings.title: Session 3: Animal Alarm (first coding session)
goals: Complete SPIKE Coding Lesson 1 and explore sensor + sound blocks
Learn how biologists detect animals
Introduce Core Value: Teamwork
activities: Recap + vocabulary (detect, program, sensor); Teamwork intro 5-10 min with EN p.7 drawing
Complete Coding Lesson 1 'Animal Alarm' in the SPIKE app Explore Unit; modify so the color changes when an animal moves in front of the sensor; write the program on EN p.12
Explore sound blocks; record a custom animal sound and trigger it on sensor detection; test with Session 2 creatures
Challenge: one sound per invented animal staged on the mat with its story
Share coding blocks learned; clean up: take EVERYTHING apart, return to storage, charge the set
deliverables: Coding Lesson 1 complete; program recorded on EN p.12

meetings.title: Session 4: Treehouse Camp (motor blocks)
goals: Complete SPIKE Coding Lesson 2 and explore motor-coding blocks
Discuss observing wildlife from treehouses
Introduce Core Value: Fun
activities: Recap + vocabulary (motor, observe, treehouse); Fun intro 5-10 min with EN p.7 drawing
Complete Coding Lesson 2 'Treehouse Camp'; change the program so the roof opens slowly; write ideas on EN p.14
Camouflage the treehouse model with SPIKE Essential pieces and place it on the mat
Challenge: program roof open 5s / close 5s repeated 2-3 times; each child shares build + code
Optional extension for fast finishers: Arctic Ride motor lesson
Clean up: disassemble everything, return to storage, charge the set
deliverables: Coding Lesson 2 complete; motor blocks used and explained

meetings.title: Session 5: Science Helpers (lifting platform) — Mid-season checkpoint 1
goals: Build the lifting platform and run/modify the provided code
Discuss how people collaborate to study the rainforest
Introduce Core Value: Innovation; halfway goals check
activities: Recap + vocabulary (platform, protect); Innovation intro 5-10 min with EN p.7 drawing
Build the lifting platform (Book 2, Bags 2 & 7 — motor, gear train, rack gear, scissor lift), add a scientist minifig, run the provided program; write ideas on EN p.16
Rebuild/fetch the Session 1 tree; adapt the lift to reach different areas of the tree
Challenge: two scientists on the platform, decide their research, reprogram to raise AND lower safely (watch table edges; take turns editing code)
HALFWAY THERE reflection on EN p.6; verify checkpoint 1: tree + lift built, building/coding skills developing, team can describe why people study rainforest biodiversity
Clean up: KEEP tree and lift assembled; charge the set
deliverables: Lift built and safely programmed; tree + lift stored assembled
Mid-season checkpoint 1 met; p.6 halfway reflection done

meetings.title: Session 6: Research Tools (sensor + hub)
goals: Build research tools and the sensor-driven research device
Learn tools/technology and jobs that study biodiversity
Introduce Core Value: Inclusion
activities: Recap + vocabulary (research, tool); Inclusion intro 5-10 min with EN p.7 drawing
Brainstorm and draw research tools; build one from prototyping pieces (Bags 9-13) and place it on the mat; test with Session 2 animals
Build the research device (Book 2, Bag 8); attach sensor + hub per Book 2; run the provided program and take turns moving it around the mat
Challenge: reprogram to activate on a different color; test on the team's animals; write findings on EN p.19
Career Connections: Wildlife Biologist and Conservation Scientist (EN pp.5, 28-29); revisit goals page
Clean up: KEEP the research device assembled; charge the set
deliverables: Research device built, coded, and stored assembled
Custom prototyped research tool on the mat

meetings.title: Session 7: Dream Treehouse — Mid-season checkpoint 2 + festival registration deadline
goals: Learn the six biodiversity careers and their tools
Design and build a treehouse/research station for scientists
COACH: festival + scrimmage registration confirmed and shared with families (TMG deadline)
activities: Recap + vocabulary (ecosystem, nature); Discovery mini-build with prototyping pieces 5-10 min
Explore jobs on EN pp.5, 28-29: wildlife biologist, conservation scientist, botanist, environmental scientist, ecologist, forestry technician
Design a treehouse where a wildlife biologist safely watches a chosen animal; write/draw on EN p.20; build it from prototyping pieces (can extend the tree model)
Build a tool/technology for the treehouse; Challenge: add a botanist + plant-study tool; optional outdoor plant walk
Share jobs + technology learnings; clean up: take EVERYTHING apart; store SPIKE and Explore sets separately
Coach: verify checkpoint 2 (hub/attachment practice, tools/jobs explored) and confirm Nov 8 scrimmage + December festival registration, details sent to families
deliverables: Mid-season checkpoint 2 met
Scrimmage + festival registered; date/details shared with families and caregivers

meetings.title: Coding consolidation + Core Values banking
goals: Strengthen the code-explanation skills two of the four model criteria depend on
Bank Core Values examples (reviewing criteria 8-9)
activities: Rebuild/rerun the lift and research-device programs; take turns modifying them (TMG: sessions may be revisited)
'Explain your code out loud' drills — each child narrates how a program makes a model move (reviewing packet hook)
Core Values micro-activity: collect concrete examples of teamwork and new skills, tagged to discovery, inclusion, innovation, impact, fun
Short surprise STEM mini-challenge in mixed pairs (event Special Activities practice)
Charge the set; confirm storage of assembled tree, lift, research device
deliverables: Every child has narrated at least one program aloud
Written bank of Core Values examples started

meetings.title: Session 8: Team Model (meeting 1 of 2)
goals: Review the team model requirements and design the model
Begin building; Core Values: Teamwork + Fun
activities: Teamwork + Fun mini-builds 5-10 min; vocabulary: model, design, label

Read the Team Model requirements aloud (EN p.23): LEGO elements only; all Explore Set parts + mat; a SPIKE-motorized part; a designed plant/animal; a rainforest job; a biodiversity-study tool/technology
Draw and LABEL the team model design on EN pp.22-23, including every member's ideas
Each member begins building an assigned part of the model (needs ALL Explore Set parts + mat)
Share design strengths; clean up: keep work-in-progress safe; return unused pieces
deliverables: Labeled team model design on EN pp.22-23
Model parts under construction

meetings.title: Session 8: Team Model (meeting 2 of 2)
goals: Finish the team model on the mat with all required elements
Motorize and code a chosen part
activities: Combine members' parts on the Explore mat; check it fits on a table and moves easily
Verify all required parts against the p.23 checklist: designed plant/animal, rainforest job, biodiversity tool/tech, whole Explore Set + mat, LEGO-only
Motorize any part with SPIKE Essential and code it using skills from Sessions 3-6
Share: demonstrate the moving part; each child points to and explains parts; discuss what to tell reviewers
Clean up: TEAM MODEL STAYS ASSEMBLED from now to the festival; return unused pieces
deliverables: Team model built, requirements verified, motorized part coded and working
Model stored assembled

meetings.title: Session 8 overflow: model refinement + code narration
goals: Polish the motorized mechanism (EN planning note: buffer meeting after Session 8)
Prepare kids to explain the model and code (reviewing criteria 4-7)
activities: Test and improve the motorized/coded part's reliability; iterate per the Engineering Design Process (Explore/Create/Test/Share)
Each child practices describing the model, the Explore Set components used creatively, which part is motorized, and how the code works
Reporter captures photos/notes of the finished model for the poster and festival
Re-check model against the p.23 requirements; confirm safe storage and transportability
deliverables: Motorized part demonstrably reliable
Every child can identify and explain model parts

meetings.title: Session 9: Team Poster (meeting 1 of 2)
goals: Plan poster content covering the team journey
Core Values: Innovation + Inclusion
activities: Innovation + Inclusion mini-builds 5-10 min; vocabulary: draft, team journey

Discuss required content: how the team worked together, what they learned about biodiversity, what they built as the team model, plus anything else — and real-world connections to people/careers/technologies (reviewing criterion 2)
Draft the poster plan on EN p.25, mining the Team Journey and Core Values notebook pages
Coach looks ahead to Session 10 reviewer questions while guiding content; decide how EACH person will talk about the poster
Sketch layout on extra drafting paper for the trifold board
deliverables: Poster content draft on EN p.25 with a section owner per child

meetings.title: Session 9: Team Poster (meeting 2 of 2)
goals: Create the poster with every team member contributing
activities: Gather trifold poster board + art supplies (coach-supplied); children make the poster themselves, coach supports only
Build the three assessed sections: what we learned about BioGlow (specific facts/ideas), real-world people/careers/technologies, and our journey (what we built, coded, and learned)
Include Core Values and Reporter's photos/notes from the season
Practice how each person introduces their section
Clean up: extra time for art supplies; store the poster somewhere safe
deliverables: Poster substantially complete and stored safely

meetings.title: Session 9 overflow: finish poster + first walk-through (hard gate)
goals: Finish the poster (Session 9 absorbed two old sessions — extra time is per the multimedia guide)
Meet the EN p.25 gate: model AND poster complete before Session 10
activities: Complete any unfinished poster sections; final art cleanup
First full poster walk-through: team rehearses presenting the journey, biodiversity learnings, and the team model to a visitor
Quick model check: still assembled, motorized part still runs
Watch poster examples in the 2019 World Festival recap (1:10) to compare and improve
deliverables: HARD GATE MET: team model and team poster both complete

meetings.title: Session 10: Prepare for Your Event
goals: Reflect on the BIOGLOW experience; plan and practice what to share at the festival
Core Value: Impact; go over the reviewing sheet and process
activities: Impact mini-build 5-10 min; guiding questions: how the model relates to the theme, can you explain the coded program, how will you show team spirit
Coach walks through the reviewing sheet and reviewing process (downloaded via TMG p.30 QR link)
Assign speaking roles so each child covers a part: what was explored, describing the model, explaining the motorizing program, presenting the poster-as-journey, reflecting on Core Values
Fill in EN p.27 'What I Will Share with Reviewers'
Full practice run of poster and model presentations; team prepares its own materials checklist (model, poster, LEGO set, device, cord, charged battery)
deliverables: EN p.27 completed by all members
Speaking roles assigned; team materials checklist written
Reviewing sheet reviewed with the team

meetings.title: Mock reviewing session 1
goals: Experience the exact 25-minute reviewing format
Baseline the team against the 9 reviewing criteria
activities: Run the full flow: welcome/introductions 2 min -> team presentation 5 min -> Q&A up to 10 min (poster, model, Core Values questions verbatim from the sheet) -> positive feedback 3 min -> reviewer deliberation 5 min
Coach plays reviewer with a printed reviewing sheet, ticking Beginning/Accomplished/Exceeds per line
Run it a second time with roles rotated; debrief between runs
List which of the 9 lines are still at 'Beginning' to target next meeting
deliverables: Completed mock reviewing sheet with per-criterion ratings

meetings.title: Targeted improvement from mock review 1
goals: Move 'Beginning' criteria toward 'Accomplished'
Tighten the 5-minute presentation
activities: Work the weakest reviewing-sheet lines: poster theme facts, real-world connections, model-theme link, Explore Set usage story, motorized-part explanation, code narration
'Explain your code out loud' drills for criterion 7 (Coding Award hinges on this)
Core Values example rehearsal: concrete teamwork moments and new skills, tagged to discovery, inclusion, innovation, impact, fun
Rehearse the 5-minute presentation against a timer
deliverables: Presentation fits 5 minutes
Fix list from mock review 1 worked through

meetings.title: Mock reviewing session 2 + Special Activities practice
goals: Re-score against the 9 criteria
Practice the event's surprise STEM activities
activities: Second full 25-minute mock reviewing session, scored on a fresh printed sheet; every child answers at least one question
Compare ratings with mock 1; celebrate lines that moved up
Surprise-problem practice: a novel mini STEM challenge in unfamiliar groupings (simulates festival Special Activities with other teams' kids)
Teamwork reflection closer mapped to Core Values words
deliverables: Second scored reviewing sheet showing improvement

meetings.title: Paperwork completion audit + outside-audience prep
goals: Verify every completion document ahead of the Oct 31 deadline
Prepare to present to guests
activities: Audit the document checklist: EN p.27 for all members, Core Values page complete, consent forms all returned, scrimmage + festival registrations confirmed, participation certificates printed, packing checklist final
Rehearse the poster and model presentations for an outside audience (TMG Session 10 option)
Confirm scrimmage-day logistics with families: time, location, how long teams stay
Short criteria drill on any remaining weak lines
deliverables: Paperwork audit list with every item checked or assigned an owner

meetings.title: Presentation to an outside audience
goals: Present model + poster to real guests before the scrimmage (TMG-suggested practice)
activities: Families/another class act as visitors; team delivers the 5-minute presentation
Guests ask reviewer-style questions from the sheet; each child answers at least one
Positive-feedback ritual (3 min) so kids experience the real format
Debrief: what felt hard, what to fix; Reporter notes feedback
deliverables: Guest feedback captured for the improvement meeting

meetings.title: Feedback fixes + FINAL paperwork sign-off
goals: Apply outside-audience feedback
Close all paperwork before the 2026-10-31 deadline
activities: Fix items from guest feedback: answer phrasing, poster tweaks, code-explanation clarity
Final paperwork sign-off: every checklist document confirmed complete — nothing may slip past Oct 31
Verify model integrity and hub charge routine
Core Values example bank final pass
deliverables: ALL season paperwork complete and signed off (deadline 2026-10-31)

meetings.title: Scrimmage rehearsal 1: full dress rehearsal
goals: Rehearse the entire scrimmage day end-to-end
activities: Teardown/transport/re-stage drill: pack and re-set the team model (with working code) and poster as if arriving at the venue
Full 25-minute mock reviewing session: introductions 2 min, presentation 5 min, Q&A 10 min, feedback 3 min
Verify the packing list: model, poster, LEGO Education set, device, charging cord, fully charged battery
Set expectations: the day is a celebration — showcase, Special Activities, reviewers visiting the table, award ceremony where every team wins an award
deliverables: Transport/re-stage procedure proven; packing list verified

meetings.title: Scrimmage rehearsal 2: scored full run
goals: Hit 'Accomplished' on all 9 criteria in a timed run
activities: Full mock reviewing session scored on the fillable/printed sheet (9 criteria x Beginning/Accomplished/Exceeds)
Every child answers at least one poster, model, or Core Values question — kids talk, not the coach
Timed 5-minute presentation; adjust who says what if over time
Target remaining 'Beginning' lines with focused mini-drills
deliverables: Scored sheet at or near 'Accomplished' on all 9 lines

meetings.title: Scrimmage rehearsal 3: final dress + confidence
goals: Lock the presentation and Q&A; end on fun
activities: Final timed 5-minute presentation + verbatim 9-question drill
Surprise STEM mini-challenge (Special Activities simulation)
Family logistics brief for Nov 8; pack everything transport-ready (model, poster, set, device, cord, charged battery)
Watch 'How to Prepare for your Festival' (1:39) and celebrate with the GoNoodle dance — HAVE FUN is the overriding goal
deliverables: Everything packed and transport-ready for Nov 8
Every child confident in their speaking part

meetings.title: SCRIMMAGE (dry-run festival — treat like the real event)
goals: Run the full festival experience: showcase, Special Activities, reviewing, celebration
activities: Showcase the team model and poster to everyone present
Participate in Special STEM Activities, collaborating with other teams' children
Reviewing session: reviewers visit the table, team presents 5 min and answers the 9 sheet questions
Attend the award ceremony; support and interact with other teams (Gracious Professionalism)
Reporter/coach capture the completed reviewing sheet feedback for the debrief
deliverables: Scrimmage completed; reviewing-sheet feedback in hand

meetings.title: Scrimmage debrief: feedback into a fix list
goals: Convert reviewer feedback into a concrete improvement backlog for the December festival
activities: Celebrate the scrimmage — what went well, favorite moments
Map reviewer feedback line-by-line to the 9 criteria; identify lines below 'Accomplished'
Build a prioritized fix list: model/code items, poster items, presentation/Q&A items
Confirm model survived transport; repair anything damaged; charge the set
deliverables: Prioritized improvement backlog mapped to the 9 reviewing criteria

meetings.title: Improvement kickoff: quick wins from scrimmage feedback
goals: Turn the freshest scrimmage feedback into visible progress while it's still exciting
Knock out the easiest items on the improvement backlog
activities: Re-read the prioritized backlog from the debrief; kids pick the quick wins to attack first
Fix small model issues from transport or reviewer comments; verify the motorized part still runs
Re-run the coded program and practice narrating any changes
Update the Core Values example bank with scrimmage-day moments (Gracious Professionalism sightings count)
deliverables: At least two backlog items closed
Model verified working post-scrimmage

meetings.title: Improvement 1: team model + code
goals: Fix model and coding items from the scrimmage backlog
activities: Improve the motorized part's reliability and, if reviewers suggested it, its ambition (motors/sensors/lights)
Re-verify the p.23 requirements after changes: designed plant/animal, rainforest job, biodiversity tool, whole Explore Set + mat, LEGO-only, motorized part
Code-narration drills on the updated program — each child explains the change
Test/improve cycle per the Engineering Design Process; keep the model assembled
deliverables: Model + code fixes from backlog complete and explainable by the kids

meetings.title: Improvement 2: poster + presentation
goals: Fix poster and presentation items from the scrimmage backlog
activities: Strengthen weak poster sections: theme facts, real-world people/careers/technologies, built/coded/learned journey
Add scrimmage photos/moments to the journey section (Reporter's captures)
Rework presentation phrasing where kids stumbled; re-balance speaking roles
Timed 5-minute run of the updated presentation
deliverables: Poster updated; presentation revised and back under 5 minutes

meetings.title: Mock reviewing 3 with improved artifacts
goals: Verify the improvements moved the scores
activities: Full 25-minute mock reviewing session with the updated model and poster, scored on a printed sheet
Compare against the scrimmage feedback line-by-line
Core Values questions drill with fresh examples including the scrimmage itself
Note anything still weak for December polish (no meeting Thanksgiving week Thursday)
deliverables: Post-improvement scored sheet; short December polish list

meetings.title: Final polish + main festival logistics
goals: Close the polish list; lock festival logistics with families
activities: Work remaining polish items from Nov 24 mock review
Confirm main festival date/time/location/duration (December, TBD) and share details with families and caregivers
Refresh EN p.27 answers to reflect the improved model and poster
Practice 2-3 sheet questions aloud per child as a stand-up drill
deliverables: Festival details communicated to families
Polish list closed

meetings.title: Main-event dress rehearsal
goals: Full festival-day rehearsal with the final artifacts
activities: Teardown/transport/re-stage drill with the final model and poster
Full 25-minute mock reviewing session: 5-min presentation + 9-question Q&A + positive-feedback ritual
Special Activities simulation and ceremony expectation-setting for kids and parents
Verify device, charging cord, and battery routine
deliverables: Festival-day procedure locked end-to-end

meetings.title: Final festival prep (flex for TBD festival date)
goals: Be fully packed and confident whatever the exact festival date
activities: Final packing-list check: team model (assembled), team poster, LEGO Education set, device, charging cord, fully charged battery
Light run: each child delivers their speaking part once; team spirit practice
Brief families: celebration format, reviewers visiting the table, every team wins one award (Challenge Solution, Team Poster, Team Model, Coding, Core Values, or Name Your Own)
If the festival falls earlier this week, this meeting becomes post-event celebration
deliverables: Team festival-ready: artifacts packed, roles rehearsed, families briefed

meetings.title: Festival-week flex meeting
goals: Support the main festival whenever it lands; keep it light and fun
activities: If pre-festival: short confidence run-through of presentation and Q&A, then team games from the Core Values/team-building bank
If post-festival: share festival stories and the award earned; start FESTIVAL TIME reflections on EN p.6
GoNoodle 'Celebrate' dance; no heavy work — fun is the goal
deliverables: Team peaked (or celebrated) for the main festival

meetings.title: Post-season wrap-up: teardown + inventory + reflection
goals: Complete the TMG post-season wrap-up
activities: Complete FESTIVAL TIME reflections on EN p.6; team reflection on the whole journey
Take apart the team model; return all SPIKE Essential elements to the set and inventory it
Decide what to do with the Explore Set elements
Kids take Engineering Notebooks home
deliverables: SPIKE Essential set inventoried; model retired; reflections done

meetings.title: Season celebration + certificates
goals: Celebrate every child and close the season
activities: Award the printed Student Participation Certificates to each team member
Celebration party with families invited; share Reporter's season photos
Final Core Values reflection: what new skills and ideas the team learned together
Coach collects interest for next season
deliverables: Certificates awarded; season closed with a celebration

points: Let's Get Started

slides.title: Team Journey
points: Explore the Challenge
Learn about Core Values
slides.tip: Set the arc up front: discover the theme, build and code a model, track it in the notebook, and share at the Explore festival.

slides.title: Team Journey: Create Team Model
points: Create Team Model
Engineering Design Process: Explore, Create, Test, Share
slides.tip: The design process has no set order — teams may explore, create, test, and share several times in a single session.

points: Make Team Poster
Celebrate at Festival

slides.title: Team Roles
points: Material Manager — gathers materials for the session and returns them at the end.
Reporter — captures the team's journey with pictures or notes to use at the festival.
Builder — assembles the LEGO models; LEGO Element Finder — locates the pieces for each build step.
Coder — operates the device and creates the programs in the app.
Researcher — writes down team questions about the theme and helps look up answers.
Adult Facilitator — a coach, teacher, or mentor who guides the team through the sessions.
slides.tip: Rotate roles so everyone tries each one; builder and coder can be doubled for pairs — add a team captain role if helpful.

slides.title: Form Your Team
points: Write your Team Name and Members names in your Engineering Notebook, page 3.
slides.tip: Form teams now and have each child record the names and team name on notebook page 3.

Write your goals in your Engineering Notebook, page 6.
slides.tip: Have students reflect on what they want to learn this season before writing their goals down.

slides.title: Core Values

INCLUSION
INNOVATION
TEAMWORK
IMPACT
FUN

slides.title: Session 1: Canopy Connections
points: I can work with my team using discovery to explore the BioGlow theme and share what I know about biodiversity.
I can work with my team to build the tree model.
I can work with my team to share about what we built.
Students share what they know about biodiversity, look at the Explore Story, build the tree model, and talk about where animals live.

slides.title: Introduction
points: Can your team provide examples of how they have used discovery?
We explore new skills and ideas.
slides.tip: Spend 5-10 minutes on the FIRST Core Values: read the discovery definition (TMG p5), then have everyone draw a discovery example in their notebook.

slides.title: Key Vocabulary
points: Biodiversity: the many different types of plant and animal life on Earth
Canopy: a giant, leafy room that covers a forest
Habitat: a plant or animal's natural home

slides.title: Guiding Questions
points: What do you know about the rainforest and biodiversity?
What does a wildlife biologist do?
What do you think is happening in the Explore Story?
slides.tip: It's okay if they don't know anything about biodiversity yet — learning is what the experience is about.

slides.title: Activity 1 Tasks
points: Look at the Explore Story on page 4.
What do you see?
What are the characters and animals doing?
slides.tip: Have students look closely at each picture and imagine what the characters and animals might be thinking or doing.

slides.title: Activity 1 Tasks
points: Share what you know about animals in rainforests with your team.
Write or draw what your team shared in your Engineering Notebook on page 8.
slides.tip: Also have the team list their goals on page 6 — the notebook gives every member space to write or draw their ideas.

slides.title: Guiding Questions
points: What are the different layers of the rainforest?
What kinds of animals live in trees?
Why do you think some animals live on the forest floor while others live high up in the canopy?
slides.tip: Talk through each question now to frame the session — students will share their thoughts with their team later.

slides.title: Activity 2 Tasks
points: Using Book 1 and Bags 1-2, work together to build the tree model.
slides.tip: Rainforest layers are on notebook page 30; the team can rearrange pieces on the tree to create a specific animal habitat.

slides.title: Activity 2 Tasks
points: Talk about what animals live on the forest floor and in the canopy.
Draw a picture of the animals your team talked about on page 9 of your Engineering Notebook.
slides.tip: Encourage each child to share what they built and explain where animals could live in the tree.

slides.title: Challenge
points: Change the tree model by moving the leaves to new places.
slides.tip: Have them draw or describe the animals they talked about; rainforest layers are on notebook page 30.

slides.title: Share
points: Share what you built.
What do you think happened in the Explore Story?
What do you know about rainforests?
What animals might live in your tree?
slides.tip: Have each team share with the whole room.

slides.title: Career Connection: Wildlife Biologist
points: A wildlife biologist is a scientist who studies wild animals and their homes.
They investigate what animals eat, how they behave, and what keeps them healthy.
Their main goal is to protect creatures and make sure their natural habitats stay safe and strong.

slides.title: Clean Up
slides.tip: Keep the tree model assembled for future sessions; a clean-up song (GoNoodle or YouTube) makes tidying fun.

slides.title: Session 2: Creature Creators
points: I can work with my team to build the animals from the Explore Set.

How will your team show your team spirit at events?
slides.tip: Talk through each question with the students and have them share their thoughts with the team.

slides.title: Share
points: Practice in front of everyone.
Show off the team poster & team model.
slides.tip: Have the team practice both their poster and model presentations in front of the whole room.

slides.title: Clean Up
slides.tip: Store the model and poster ready to transport, and check you have the device, charging cord, and a fully charged battery for the event.
